quest.title: Pale Fire
quest.description: A magical Plume of Purifying Light has formed on the Fravashi Tree. One wonders what secrets it holds within...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x25000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: The Pari once scattered across the land seem to have all returned.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Great work indeed, as expected of the Yasnapati whom Sorush has chosen.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I'll take that as a compliment, Elder Zurvan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, the Vourukasha Oasis already seems a lot more lively.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've also fixed that giant hole in the sky. Everything here should recover in just no time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, now that Paimon thinks about it, if Pari are born from the water, shouldn't you be called "Hydri" or something?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hey! Don't try to give us one of your stupid nicknames, Pale Floater!

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Hehe, that does remind me of something from the distant past...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: A long, long time ago, a slew of Oceanids from foreign lands once traveled here, in spite of the many obstacles.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: To arrive here, not only did they have to withstand the scorching desert, but they also had to face rampant monsters. For those water creatures, that journey must have been extremely tormenting.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: They seemed to have come for their deceased god, only to find that what they were looking for wasn't here.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: After seeing the Harvisptokhm, they soon dispersed and left.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Since then, the legend of the Oceanids spread, and many outlanders traveled along the road they once ventured, looking to uncover their secrets.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Although it started out as a rumor, as time passed by, the route itself has been endowed with the meaning of sacrificing oneself in pursuit of pure innocence.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Even after the Vourukasha Oasis was sealed off from the outside world, their pilgrimage still lasted for quite a long time.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Perhaps for them, the journey is more important than the destination.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: One might also argue that the process of striving towards a goal yields more significance than merely sacrificing yourself once and for all.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hey! Why does it always come back to me!?

choices.text: Hope it's not too long a story...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Well, if it isn't Sorush and her Yasnapati... My, even Paimon's here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What do you mean "even"? That's offensive!

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: From the looks on your faces, you've found something interesting, haven't you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not sure if "interesting" is the right word...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Zurvan about the Fravashi Tree...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: I see. Now, where should I begin?

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: What you just described is indeed a Fravashi Tree that a Pari has transformed into. But as for what resides within such trees, I believe it more accurate to call them "fragmented memories" than "residual Pari."

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: It is quite akin, in fact, to that Plume of Purifying Light you obtained, which contains memories that cannot return to the earth.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: We are born from the Vourukasha Oasis, and we shall return there eventually.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The god safeguarding this place is rejected by the time flowing throughout this land, and so are we.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: That said, this is also what we wish for. After all, it is our purpose to keep the defilement from flowing into the land along with us.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: And in the Amrita Pool, we get to wash off whatever filthiness that once tainted us.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: By offering that Plume of Purifying Light to the Amrita Pool, you will enable the Pari to return to the Vourukasha Oasis once again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, that means we did a good deed this time, right?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmph. You grow ever so haughty, Pale Floater, as if this were not all thanks to my great power.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you're pretty amazing too, Sorush!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: That's more like it... though I need no compliments from you so long as my Yasnapati is present.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Speaking of Yasnapati, now that you've more or less accepted this title, that indeed makes you the perfect candidate for the ritual.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: In ancient times, the human warriors who walked with Pari would hold a ritual of purification for the Pari scattered in the desert, so as to bring them back to the Vourukasha Oasis.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: And those who have established a special bond with the Pari have been addressed as "Yasnapati" ever since.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? That's entirely different from what Sorush told us!

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Is that so? Well, she was bound to get something right by luck eventually. As for you, Yasnapati, you now shoulder the responsibility to help the Pari that have yet to return.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: If you encounter other Fravashi Trees, please bring the Plumes of Purifying Light they have formed back to the Vourukasha Oasis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we'd help them even if you didn't ask!

choices.text: So do the ones we offered to the Amrita Pool...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Plumes of Purifying Light are derived from Simurgh's Khvarena. And we Pari originated due to the contact between Khvarena and Amrita.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: That is why we are also known as the descendants of Khvarena.
